arguments.prompt:
Run the newly agreed local Voronoi experiment in this existing cloud workspace. The user explicitly approved cloud execution now. This is a fresh experiment from the current chat “Determine whether contour dots form,” not a continuation of the old hexagon-vertex annealing run. Preserve the old runs and documents; use a separate directory such as work/voronoi25 and outputs/voronoi25.

First verify actual cloud execution and inspect the recovered data already present here. Return concrete progress as work completes. Finish the 25-round experiment, verify it, and return results rather than stopping after a plan or an acknowledgment. Keep computation interruptible and checkpoint each completed round. If execution is genuinely unavailable, report the actual error promptly.

DATA AND INITIAL CONFIGURATION
Use the recovered original Manhattan pickup records, their existing kilometer coordinate system, and the verified Manhattan main-island boundary. The recovered bundle is Manhattan_Later_Compact_Recovery.zip, persistent ID libfile_dc84879b89c08191b3fb5efe83d086ad; you previously recovered and hash-checked it here. Relevant historical paths include Manhattan_Pickups_2015-01-15_0800-0815.json, work/median100/input.json, work/median100/initialize.py, work/median100/build.py, work/verified38/main_island_km.geojson, work/verified38/main_island_lonlat.geojson. Use existing local recovered files before requesting any transfer.
Historical provenance: 5,986 pickup records, with duplicates retained. Previously 5,983 lay within the nonconvex main-island boundary. The region for THIS experiment is P = convex hull of that full main-island region. Reassess containment in P and report any exclusions; do not automatically discard the former three outside indices (309,4705,5212). Treat coincident pickup records as separate unit-weight observations.
Initialize exactly 100 distinct regularly spaced centers inside P. No random center placement. Use a deterministic triangular lattice fitted inside the hull, preferably in the existing coordinate orientation. Choose spacing/offset deterministically to obtain exactly 100 interior sites and save those exact coordinates and initialization method. The old grid-building code may be reused if it supplies suitable regular centers, but the old optimized mesh vertices are not the new initial sites. Use a documented random seed only for the per-round permutations.

SINGLE-CENTER STEP — IMPLEMENT THESE FORMULAS
At the start of a step, calculate bounded Euclidean Voronoi cells V_j for the current sites c_j in convex P. Neighbors share a positive-length edge, not just a vertex. Choose the next existing center i from the round's permutation. Let N_i be its current neighbors, S_i = {i} union N_i. Count points by closest center, tie broken by smallest center index. For j in S_i, A_j is current area, M_j is current dot count, rho_j = M_j/A_j, W_j = M_j. These rho_j are the coefficients used throughout this single movement calculation. Do not use individual dot locations to choose direction, step size, geometric capping, or acceptance after these counts are computed.

For each j in N_i let ell_ij and m_ij be the shared edge length and midpoint, and define:
b_ij = (ell_ij / ||c_i-c_j||) (m_ij-c_i)
g_i = sum_{j in N_i} (W_i-W_j) b_ij.
This is the local gradient of E_i(q)=1/2 sum_{j in S_i} rho_j A_j(q)^2, where only c_i is replaced by q.
If the gradient vanishes, leave c_i unchanged.
Otherwise:
u_i = -g_i/||g_i||
a_i = sum_{j in N_i} dot(b_ij,u_i)
a_j = -dot(b_ij,u_i) for j in N_i
s0 = ||g_i|| / sum_{j in S_i} rho_j a_j^2.
This s0 is the minimizer for linearized AREAS; do not describe it as the exact geometric line-search optimum. With nonzero g the denominator should be positive; handle numerical degeneracy explicitly and record it.
Calculate c_i' = c_i + s*u_i. Use the proposed s0, shortening it only as necessary to remain inside P, avoid reaching another center exactly on the forward ray within the proposed move, or avoid acquiring a neighbor outside the initial N_i. Losing an initial neighbor is allowed. The constraints apply throughout the straight move, not just to the endpoint. Use a documented small numerical clearance before an event and record actual and proposed lengths and limiting event. If already at a limiting event and unable to advance, record a zero-length constrained step.
No extra global objective, annealing, Lloyd/centroid movement, dot-count acceptance test, or arbitrary trust-radius reduction is part of this protocol. Recompute the cells and local densities for the next step. Only one center changes in each step.

GEOMETRIC CAPPING — IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS ARE YOUR RESPONSIBILITY
The user agreed to the constraints, while leaving numerical implementation open. Robust event calculations are preferred to endpoint-only tests, which can miss an intermediate violation.
One useful derivation to verify and use: for a nonneighbor k at the beginning of a step, its current cell equals its cell with site i removed. Until the first new neighbor appears, that cell is unchanged. The moving site becomes a new neighbor of k when it becomes strictly closer than c_k at some vertex v of that fixed convex cell. Along p(t)=c_i+t*u_i the test is the quadratic
f_v,k(t)=||c_i+t*u_i-v||^2-||c_k-v||^2.
The first entry into f<0 over vertices of all initially nonneighbor cells gives the first possible new-neighbor event. Tangency alone does not create a positive-length shared edge. This includes region-boundary vertices. Verify this event calculation against recomputed geometry on representative steps; account for initial degeneracies and numerical tolerances.
Region exit is ray/convex-polygon intersection; collision is only a fixed center lying exactly on the forward ray, using appropriate numerical tolerance. Do not prohibit merely getting near an off-ray center.

ROUNDS AND MEASURES
Run exactly 25 rounds. Each round uses a fresh uniformly random permutation of indices 0..99 (equivalently 1..100), visiting every center exactly once. Record the seed and permutations. The trial's end at 25 rounds is not a claim of convergence.
Before round 1 and after each complete round r=1..25, calculate current point-count weights W_i and current clipped adjacency N_i. Let d_ij=abs(W_i-W_j), in NUMBER OF DOTS, not percentages. For each cell:
Gmax_i=max_{j in N_i} d_ij
Gavg_i=mean_{j in N_i} d_ij
Gmed_i=median_{j in N_i} d_ij.
Report six quantities across cells:
max_i Gmax_i, max_i Gavg_i, max_i Gmed_i,
median_i Gmax_i, median_i Gavg_i, median_i Gmed_i.
Medians use the arithmetic mean of the two middle values for even sample sizes. Compute each column's median independently. Save all 26 records (initial + 25 rounds). Use the actual post-round point assignments for evaluation; no smoothing or modeled area weights in these reported measures.

VALIDATION AND DELIVERABLES
Check gradient and area-rate formulas by finite differences at a few nondegenerate configurations; include the simple two-center unit-square test (centers .25,.5 and .75,.5, counts9 and1) whose uncapped proposed distance for center1 is .8 to the left, requiring a region cap. Check cap detection, distinct in-region centers, convex cells, coverage, shared-edge consistency, total assigned count, and all permutation membership. These are targeted numerical correctness checks, not a separate research project.
Complete the run without modifying the agreed rule if balance worsens or the no-new-neighbor restriction causes stagnation. Report what happened honestly.
Save: runnable source; exact input/projection/provenance manifest; initial and round25 centers and cells; per-round checkpoints and six-measure CSV/JSON; per-step logs of movement and constraint hits; clear before/after maps on equal axes with site markers, cell boundaries, and dot-count labels; plots of all six measures versus rounds. Use an interactive view only if easily supported; static readable figures suffice.
In your final response, include the initial/final six numbers in a compact table, moved/blocked step counts, active constraint statistics, actual validation results, and links/native images of outputs. Include a compact JSON result summary inline so this parent chat can retrieve it via read_thread. A portable output bundle is useful for import back to the Mac; provide a persistent file identifier or real transfer mechanism if available, since cloud sandbox links alone are not local file paths. Do not contact other chats.

content.text: ok, except each round must be a random permutation, and do a few rounds (say 25) and then we inspect some measure.  let's discuss measures: maximal/average/median gap between a cell and adjacent cells.  1. maximum for all cells. 2. values of the median cell in each of these dimensions

items.text:
Agreed: **25 rounds, each using a fresh random permutation of the existing centers**, with each center moving once per round.

For measurement, let \(W_i\) be cell \(i\)’s current dot count and define the gap \(d_{ij}=|W_i-W_j|\). For each cell:
\[
G_i^{\max}=\max_{j\in N_i}d_{ij},\qquad
G_i^{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac1{|N_i|}\sum_{j\in N_i}d_{ij},\qquad
G_i^{\mathrm{med}}=\operatorname{median}_{j\in N_i}d_{ij}.
\]

Your proposal gives **six measures**:

| Across cells | Maximum neighbor gap | Average neighbor gap | Median neighbor gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Maximum | \(\max_i G_i^{\max}\) | \(\max_i G_i^{\mathrm{avg}}\) | \(\max_i G_i^{\mathrm{med}}\) |
| Median | \(\operatorname{median}_i G_i^{\max}\) | \(\operatorname{median}_i G_i^{\mathrm{avg}}\) | \(\operatorname{median}_i G_i^{\mathrm{med}}\) |

Each column is ranked separately. With 100 cells, its median is the average of the 50th and 51st sorted values.

We can record these initially and after every round. These definitions measure gaps in **numbers of dots**.

For the first trial, I propose:

- **100 centers**, regularly spaced inside the convex hull.
- Update centers **in fixed index order**, one at a time.
- Run **one complete pass**, then inspect the map and neighbor weight gaps before deciding the termination rule.

We’ll use the **convex hull of Manhattan**: the smallest convex polygon containing the existing Manhattan region,
\[
P=\operatorname{conv}(M).
\]
This fills its indentations and holes, including some surrounding water.
